text: Telltale settlement and coverage structure: settlement authority above $500,000 requires sign-off from the CFO (Cormac Brightwater). The self-insured retention is $750,000 per claim. Insurance liaison Thaddeus Wren handles coverage. The GC is Marguerite Salvesen.

Telltale reporting and billing requirements: monthly written updates and a call after significant events; initial assessment within 45 days; five business days' notice before filing any motion; phase budgets with variance explanations for variances over 10%; no more than two timekeepers at depositions; communications go to the GC (Marguerite Salvesen) with the insurance liaison (Thaddeus Wren) copied; litigation holds are required on relevant product documents.

Telltale expert and regulatory requirements: consult the client before engaging any testifying expert, offering three names per discipline with prior testimony notes. The regulatory affairs group (led by Odalys Fennimore) must review every expert report before service, with ten business days allowed. The client was in a regulatory inspection on its next-generation lead and wants filings to avoid characterizing failure rates beyond what is needed.

Expert report process for Telltale: route regulatory-affairs comments on expert reports through counsel and log what is sent so the exchange stays protected work product. Have the expert deliver a near-final draft early enough to fit the client's ten-business-day review before the service deadline, and confirm that any draft-protection stipulation covers this review.

Telltale requires its General Counsel (Marguerite Salvesen) to discuss proposed testifying experts before anyone is signed, and to receive fee quotes before engagement. Clear each expert with her first, because expert fees are the largest budget swing item.

Telltale's regulatory affairs group (under Odalys Fennimore) must read every defense expert report before service to check consistency with regulatory submissions. Allow about two weeks for the review. Comments go through counsel to the expert, not directly. Schedule expert draft delivery early enough to fit the review before the service date.

Telltale settlement instruction: listen if plaintiff raises resolution, but give no number. Telltale will not authorize or convey any offer, in any form, until the treating physician has been deposed. After that deposition, send the General Counsel an assessment and recommended range. Authority above $500,000 requires approval from CFO Cormac Brightwater, which the GC arranges. At any mediation, attend to listen and do not put a number on the table unless the testimony helps, and write to the GC right after the transcript arrives.

Telltale wants nothing about its settlement thinking or claims reserves to reach a mediator or anyone outside the case team. Reserve figures are for the team only. The client wants to approve any mediator before the firm agrees, and to confirm the mediation is confidential and cannot be used against Telltale in other cases.

Telltale defends several ArcLine cases and wants no material from one case to appear in another. Keep sensitive produced documents in restricted folders, do not use them in other matters or share them with other company counsel, and confirm in writing who on the team has access. The same applies to mediation statements and any numbers discussed. The GC also instructed that no strategy or work product be shared with other Telltale counsel unless she asks.

Telltale asks that settlement hints from plaintiff's counsel be acknowledged politely and kept out of any correspondence not marked as a settlement communication. Mark any settlement-related correspondence accordingly, and do not let informal resolution requests sit in ordinary discovery email threads.
